smells.finding: score_arm.py's score() (still ~65 lines, unchanged in shape by this rework's fixes) remains one function doing record-walking, per-call classification (shape/usage/state/other) and far-side detection together with several co-mutated counters. Carried forward from attempt-1's pass, unchanged by the loop/argparse fixes -- those fixes were made inside engine_invocations() and the shape-error branch without decomposing score() itself. Not a blocker (it is a disposable measurement instrument, not shipped product code), but the same observation stands: isolating per-invocation counting into its own small, unit-testable function would likely have caught the loop undercount before publication rather than after a BLOCK.

control_scorer.py's use()/res()/rec() helpers build synthetic tool_use/tool_result records structurally similar to score_arm.py's own walk() parsing, but they are test-fixture builders (the inverse operation -- constructing records vs consuming them), not a second copy of score_arm.py's classification logic. control_scorer.py imports score() from score_arm.py rather than reimplementing it, which is the correct shape for a positive-control harness.

score()'s return value is a plain dict of ~11 co-varying counters rather than a small result type/dataclass, which is borderline primitive-obsession territory, but every consumer (assert_dc1.py, control_scorer.py, MEASUREMENT.md's re-derivation commands with --json) treats it as a flat, self-describing record and the field names are stable and documented in the docstring -- judged absent rather than flagged since a dataclass would not change any behavior or catch any of the four corrections found this gate.

Both the loop fix and the argparse-double-count fix are contained entirely within engine_invocations() and the shape/usage branch of score() respectively -- one function each, one file, no ripple into assert_dc1.py, control_scorer.py or the arm runner.
control_scorer.py's 7 controls are each tied to a real counter that reports zero in the real arms (per its own stated purpose) -- no speculative extension points or unused generality.

score_arm.py, control_scorer.py and MEASUREMENT.md all carry long prose comments/docstrings explaining WHY a classification or correction choice was made (e.g. why the loop correction takes max(static, runtime-marks), why a bare 'usage:' block with no error line is still a shape rejection, why the server log is corroboration-only), and MEASUREMENT.md's new Revision note explains the review-driven correction history in full.

override.repo_standard: CREW_CONTEXT.md 'Verification Discipline' + global-everyone.md 'Pin a claim to the revision you read it at' -- this repo's convention is to make measurement/decision rationale explicit and durable in the artifact, especially for a one-off instrument a second party must independently re-derive from and for a write-up whose own numbers changed under review.
override.reason: These are decision-rationale comments for an independent auditor (this review), not comments compensating for unclear code that should have been refactored instead -- this exact review used them to check the corrections (r7-r10) and to trace the provenance of the productive-invocation decomposition (r10). They earn their keep.
